scope: Theorem 4.1 (The two formal affine fields) of the manuscript “Entropy equality and local symmetry in negative curvature” (preprints/Entropy-equality-and-local-symmetry-in-negative-curvature-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 339 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8658ab8209a8aa0c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 14-15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At every point of a conull invariant set there are formal affine fields Au, As of horizontal m-covectors with the following properties. (i) Their values contain u and w, respectively. At the center, the exterior product of any element of Au with any element of As equals the fixed nonzero exterior product u ∧ w. (ii) The fields are equivariant under f, changes of section, and flip, with the same constant and height multipliers as u, w. In a flow box their height dependences are e−hτ and ehτ . (iii) On each entire typical strong stable or strong unstable leaf, every ambient Taylor coefficient has a smooth representative agreeing almost everywhere with the regular construction. These representatives are holonomic: differentiating along the leaf gives the corresponding higher ambient coefficients. The analogous assertion holds on typical weak leaves, using flow transport. 14 (iv) At every finite order the local representatives, their bounds, and positive radii can be chosen measurably. On compact plaque subboxes one may restrict to positive-measure families with uniform finite-order bounds. No common convergence radius for all orders is asserted.
